summary:
The record of revision r4 is sound after repairs. All 52 decisions are settled, and no section, decision text, or term says that a decision is open or that the maintainer must select. I changed 4 section files and no JSON file. The strict build has no warning, `check.mjs` ends with "All checks passed.", and the page has no console error and no sideways scroll at 1440 px and 400 px.

Skills loaded after `git remote -v` (origin is github.com/ariakit/visonaut): `ariakit-general-workflow`, `ariakit-general-code-style`. No visonaut skill is installed.

The main result is point 3. With all 52 answers read as one design, I found 10 places where the two new answers meet an earlier answer. The three that matter most:

1. **D-OPS-04 changes the base of D-CODE-02.** D-CODE-02 removes the comparison Worker because "the Submit job decodes each capture". With no file check, a pull request of an account with push access can replace the Submit job. Then nothing decodes the images of that run. The only server check is the size and the digest:

```ts
// apps/web/src/api/workflow-owned.ts:1042
if (bytes.byteLength !== image.bytes || (await sha256(bytes)) !== image.digest) {
  throw new SecurityError("image_mismatch", 422, "The image digest or size differs.");
}
```

2. **The service part of D-OPS-04 needs no cutover.** The record says "one CLI release and one last pin cutover". The three comparisons are in the service only. CLI 0.5.4 checks only the form of the variable, so it still passes when the service compares nothing:

```ts
// packages/cli/src/signed-context.ts:24-28
const workflowSha = environment.VISONAUT_WORKFLOW_SOURCE_SHA;
if (!record(claims) || !/^[a-f0-9]{40}$/.test(workflowSha ?? "") || claims.job_workflow_sha !== environment.GITHUB_SHA || ...
```

So the service can stop the comparisons first, in an ordinary deployment, with no failure window. Nobody built that order.

3. **Two settled answers disagree about one file.** D-CODE-04 says that 5 files with 12,242 words stay in `docs/`. One of them is `operations/adapter-service-pins.md` (1,857 words), the pin runbook that the answer to D-OPS-04 removes. After the last cutover, 4 files with 10,385 words stay.

Each finding is now in the record in one or two sentences. Section 15 has 7,220 reader words against 7,222 in r3. To stay below r3, I cut the second code example (the row, which is a copy of section 40), three history sentences, and the long labels of one table.

The list "What still needs your word" still has 11 items. I merged two items, added one that the record requires and the list missed (two log contents), and corrected one (the maintainer reads the two GitHub App settings himself: they are not production reads).

Files changed (all below /Users/diegohaz/Developer/visonaut/.claude/worktrees/serialized-dazzling-pixel/apps/lab/audit/content/sections/): 15-your-answers.html, 30-access-trust.html, 40-data-storage.html (2 rows of the D-DATA-01 list, outside the D-DATA-02 part), 45-code-ci-docs.html. Not changed by me: record.json, decisions.json, terms.json, findings.json, 70-design-lab.html (byte-equal to its r3 copy), and the D-OPS-04 part of section 35.
verdict: sound-after-repairs. Status claims: correct in each section, in decisions.json, and in terms.json. The two new settled answers agree with their research, number by number. 10 cross-decision findings are stated in the record, and 6 of them need the coordinator because they touch a settledAnswer or a rationale that I must not change. Feedback mechanics: all cases pass. Section 15 is 2 words shorter than its r3 copy.

crossDecisionFindings.finding: D-OPS-04 lets a pull request of an account with push access replace the Submit job. D-CODE-02 removes the comparison Worker because the Submit job decodes each image, and its settled answer says "The contract then says that the Submit job is the validator." For a run with a replaced Submit job, nothing decodes the images. D-AUTH-04 counts settings that the same job sends. The record said this only for the pixel count and for D-AUTH-04.
crossDecisionFindings.evidence: apps/web/src/api/workflow-owned.ts:1038-1044: in local mode the upload checks only `bytes.byteLength !== image.bytes || (await sha256(bytes)) !== image.digest`. The decode call at :1066-1089 runs only for a mode that the service does not give. Section 45: "This is the only server check of the image bytes." The context of D-CODE-02 said: "if the decode in the Submit job is sufficient for you. If the service must check the bytes, select the last option." The maintainer answered that before D-OPS-04 had no file check.
crossDecisionFindings.action: Stated: new row "The Submit job" in the fit table of section 15, and a note "Revision r4" before the D-CODE-02 panel in section 45. What stays: size at most 2 MiB, digest, `nosniff`, sandbox policy, and the same 5 accounts. For the coordinator: the settledAnswer of D-CODE-02 does not name this limit.

crossDecisionFindings.finding: The record says that D-OPS-04 "needs one CLI release and one last pin cutover" and puts all of it in step 9. Only the service compares the three pinned values. The service can stop the comparisons first, in an ordinary deployment. CLI 0.5.4 still passes, so there is no failure window, and each workflow edit of Ariakit after that deployment is a normal pull request. The CLI release is necessary only to delete the variable line (app.yml:234).
crossDecisionFindings.evidence: packages/cli/src/signed-context.ts:24-31 and bundle-submit.ts:81 check only that VISONAUT_WORKFLOW_SOURCE_SHA has 40 hex characters and that `job_workflow_sha === GITHUB_SHA`. The comparisons are in the service: packages/security/src/oidc.ts:157-206 and :207 (`request.plan_digest`), apps/web/src/api/workflow-owned.ts:297-331 (`body.planDigest !== sourceDigest`) and :500-501 (`isTrustedWorkflowExecutor`), workflow-reconcile.ts:200-215. From code reading. Nobody built or ran it.
crossDecisionFindings.action: Stated in the fit row "CLI releases" with the label Counted from code and the words "Nobody built that order." D-OPS-04 stays in step 9 of the demo. For the coordinator: the rationale and option 1 of D-OPS-04 say "one last pin cutover", which this order makes unnecessary.

crossDecisionFindings.finding: The cost that D-RUN-03 removes is much smaller with pages of rows. Its measured gain is 455 ms for one review read (680 to 225 ms, two files of 12 MB). With pages of rows, the checks that it skips cost about 40 ms for one page. Its cost did not change: a changed trust rule, its own tests, effort M.
crossDecisionFindings.evidence: Section 40, table #data-inventory-page-size and the text below it: a read of 2,000 rows with the digest check is 4.2 to 8.2 ms, the canonical check adds 4.5 to 14.1 ms, and the profile digests add about 32 ms (estimate). All in Node. The record already said "measure one review read again before D-RUN-03".
crossDecisionFindings.action: Stated in the fit row "The inventory reader" with the label Estimate. The read-only trace of production for D-RUN-03 stays in the list, but it now measures a read that step 5 replaces.

crossDecisionFindings.finding: D-DATA-04 keeps the inventories, and its cost was "most of the estimate of 1.27 USD each month after 12 months". That estimate uses 11.7 to 12.2 MB for each run. With pages of rows a new inventory has 1.61 MB, so this cost is 7.5 times lower for new runs. Released runs lose no page: "Inventories and bookkeeping rows stay", and the deletion uses the retention pins in D1, not the inventory.
crossDecisionFindings.evidence: Section 40: "Capture list as rows: 1.61 MB" against 12.15 MB (measured, prototype). packages/service/src/run-admission.ts:636-642 writes the inherited-by pins from D1 values.
crossDecisionFindings.action: Stated in the D-DATA-04 row of the table "Where your answer differs", with the label Estimate.

crossDecisionFindings.decisions: D-DATA-02 with D-DATA-01 (alert for a large inventory)
crossDecisionFindings.finding: The settled answer of D-DATA-01 makes the alert "a read of the size that the run row already holds", at 80% of the 16 MiB limit (about 4,200 captures). With pages, the 16 MiB limit is gone and the size column names the index (913 bytes). The alert must read the capture count against the stated limit (80% of about 20,000 is 16,000).
crossDecisionFindings.evidence: packages/service/src/run-admission.ts:644: `UPDATE visonaut_runs SET inventory_key=?,inventory_digest=?,inventory_bytes=?,capture_count=?`. The run row holds both values. Section 40 says it at the end of the D-DATA-02 part. Section 15 did not.
crossDecisionFindings.action: Stated in the row of the table of forms in section 15. For the coordinator: the word "size" in the settledAnswer of D-DATA-01.

crossDecisionFindings.finding: One row of the accepted list of D-DATA-01 keeps the sorted reference list in the isolate, so that 27 inventory reads become 23. That reader answers the requests of CLI 0.5.4 (200 captures in each answer). The CLI release of D-DATA-02 replaces these requests: one request reads one stored page. So this row is work for the time from step 3 to step 9 only.

crossDecisionFindings.action: Stated in that row of the D-DATA-01 list in section 40.

crossDecisionFindings.decisions: D-DATA-02 with the compatibility part and D-RUN-02
crossDecisionFindings.finding: At the change of the stored form, a run that is in review needs a new Submit. Section 40 says it. The settled rationale and section 15 said only that older runs lose their capture list. The compatibility part names the active run of an open pull request as not safe to drop.
crossDecisionFindings.evidence: Section 40, #data-inventory-cost: "An older run loses its capture list, and a run that is in review at the change needs a new Submit."
crossDecisionFindings.action: Stated in the D-DATA-02 row of the table of one-time writes in section 15.

crossDecisionFindings.finding: The wait of D-OPS-05 is for the limit of 5 active runs. D-DATA-02 adds one more refusal, a run above the capture limit, which needs a person as the size stop does. Today the refusal text is the same for each cause (section 35), so the CLI needs a separate error code to stop at once and not wait.
crossDecisionFindings.evidence: D-OPS-05 rationale: the wait "does not help the size stop, which needs a person". Section 35: "The text and the alert are the same for the size limit and for the limit of 5 active runs". The record does not say where the reason of the D-DATA-02 refusal shows.
crossDecisionFindings.action: Stated in 7 words in the D-OPS-05 row ("or the capture limit of D-DATA-02"). The error code is for the coordinator.

crossDecisionFindings.finding: The run approval is measured to 3,832 changes, which is the largest run of today. D-DATA-02 raises the stated limit of one run to about 20,000 captures. One run approval of 20,000 changes writes about 100,000 rows in one transaction (5 for each change), and nobody measured it.
crossDecisionFindings.evidence: Section 60: "1 transaction. 18 statements in the service call, for 246 targets and for 3,832", and 5 rows for each target.
crossDecisionFindings.action: Not in the record, because section 15 has no room. For the coordinator: the measurement in a Worker that sets the capture limit can include one run approval of that size.
